verified.role: Business authority for Faber Capital Resources / Real Estate Capital Resources (RECR) program direction and investor capital-path conversations.
verified.approach: Transaction-first capital-path guidance: evaluate the property, plan, and exit, then match private-lender financing options. RECR is a broker/connector — not automatically the direct funder.
verified.focus: Business-purpose financing conversations for non-owner-occupied residential investment property — principally 1–4 units.
verified.method: Slow the conversation enough to get real numbers: property, budget or income, timing, and exit. Package a complete file so capital partners can respond to facts — not hope. Path matching is deal-led, not brochure-led.
verified.exclusions: Not the current launch sweet spot: commercial/office CRE, mobile homes, and owner-occupied primary-residence loans. Joint-venture equity is not a standard launch product and is not marketed as RECR’s differentiator.
verified.geographyNote: Site authority markets: Cleveland / Northeast Ohio and Fort Lauderdale / South Florida. Lender availability can vary by state and by capital partner.
narrative: William M. Faber leads the capital-path conversation at Real Estate Capital Resources (also known as Faber Capital Resources). The work is practical: investors bring a property and a plan; RECR helps identify which private-capital path is worth discussing and what belongs in a complete file.

The launch universe is residential investment — fix-and-flip, purchase-and-rehab, bridge, rental/DSCR hold, ground-up construction, and small multifamily within 2–4 units — always as a broker/connector matching paths, not as a promise that RECR itself is the funder.

Public biography on this site stays limited to facts that can be supported. Tenure dates, licenses, volume claims, and lender-specific numeric thresholds publish only when Bill/Richard approve them from primary sources — never from design placeholders.

transactions.situation: Investor under contract on a dated SFR with deferred mechanicals and a 90-day rehab plan.
transactions.capitalNeed: Acquisition plus staged renovation capital with a defined sale exit.
transactions.structureArranged: Short-term private-lender fix-and-flip path matched after cost-to-ARV and scope review.
transactions.challenge: Initial ARV was retail list pricing; path only worked after comps were rebuilt to finished condition.
transactions.result: Capital path identified; file packaged for private-lender review with draw schedule aligned to work stages.

transactions.situation: Stabilized rental after light rehab; investor wanted permanent cash-flow financing rather than short-term debt.
transactions.capitalNeed: DSCR-style rental financing evaluated on property income versus full debt service.
transactions.structureArranged: Rental / DSCR path matched after PITIA-inclusive coverage math and reserve discussion.
transactions.challenge: First coverage draft omitted insurance reality; file only held once full payment stack was modeled.
transactions.result: Path fit confirmed for hold strategy; investor submitted complete rent and expense package.

transactions.purpose: Short-term acquisition bridge to permanent takeout
transactions.situation: Investor needed to close quickly while a DSCR refinance package was still assembling.
transactions.capitalNeed: Temporary capital with a named refinance exit date.
transactions.structureArranged: Bridge path sequenced to a planned rental/DSCR takeout after stabilization.
transactions.challenge: Soft exit risk — permanent loan was assumed, not underwritten; exit documentation had to be made concrete first.
transactions.result: Bridge conversation proceeded only after takeout checklist and timeline were written down.

transactions.purpose: Ground-up build for sale or permanent takeout
transactions.situation: Lot under contract with preliminary plans and a GC quote that needed line-item discipline.
transactions.capitalNeed: Construction capital structured around plans, budget, draws, and completion exit.
transactions.structureArranged: Ground-up path packaging: budget, builder credibility, draw milestones, sale/refinance exit.
transactions.challenge: Contingency and soft costs were understated; build schedule did not leave room for takeout.
transactions.result: Revised construction package prepared before private-lender construction desk review.

transactions.purpose: Acquisition of 2–4 unit for cash-flow hold
transactions.situation: Buyer targeting a fourplex with mixed unit rents and deferred exterior work.
transactions.capitalNeed: Small multifamily investment financing within the 1–4 unit universe.
transactions.structureArranged: 2–4 unit path with DSCR-style income review and unit-level rent matrix.
transactions.challenge: Seller T-12 expenses looked incomplete; insurance and vacancy needed re-underwriting before path fit.
transactions.result: Unit economics rebuilt; file ready for rental-style private-lender conversation.

transactions.purpose: Purchase plus major renovation in one capital plan
transactions.situation: Heavy rehab scope (systems + layout) with hold-or-sell exit still undecided at contract.
transactions.capitalNeed: Combined acquisition and rehab budget with draw mechanics.
transactions.structureArranged: Purchase-and-rehab path: basis, line-item budget, contribution, and exit evaluated together.
transactions.challenge: Purchase only worked if rehab was free; budget and ARV support had to be rebuilt before leverage talk.
transactions.result: Honest capital plan assembled; private-lender options scoped without fixed marketing percentages.

transactions.situation: Investor with a defined flip timeline and association document package in progress.
transactions.capitalNeed: Short-term private capital for purchase and light rehab.
transactions.structureArranged: Fix-and-flip path contingent on association eligibility and defensible finished comps.
transactions.challenge: Association reserves and project rules delayed underwriting more than the paint scope.
transactions.result: Eligibility checklist completed before capital-path matching continued.

transactions.situation: Seasoned investor pulling liquidity while keeping the asset as a rental.
transactions.capitalNeed: DSCR cash-out subject to coverage after the larger payment.
transactions.structureArranged: Rental/DSCR refinance conversation with cash-flow and reserve scrutiny.
transactions.challenge: Cash-out payment pushed coverage thin until rent support and expenses were scrubbed.
transactions.result: Revised ask matched to property income reality before lender introduction.

testimonials.quote: The path conversation started with my numbers and exit, not a product brochure. That is what I needed before we talked private capital.
DSCR only made sense once taxes and insurance were in the payment. The review caught that before I wasted a week.
Unit-level rents and expenses were treated seriously. The fourplex conversation stayed inside 2–4 unit reality.
Clear on what RECR is — capital-path guidance and matching — not a fantasy rate card.
